purpose: Implement the existing EG-CORRECT, EG-FAULT, and EG-INTEGRITY registry runners for the active xtask tooling scope without changing product behavior or Qualification Cell state.

change.public_seam: cargo xtask quality returned verdict and retained target/quality/evidence attempt

dependency_review.necessity: Rust std does not expose safe descriptor-relative create, open, link, rename, unlink, directory enumeration, private-process-group creation, or group-wide termination APIs on all four registered macOS and Linux hosts. rustix is scoped only to xtask and supplies the safe I/O-owned and process-group wrappers needed to close validation/use races and terminate fixture descendants without a Positron unsafe boundary.

direct.license: Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception OR Apache-2.0 OR MIT
direct.security: The boundary uses rustix OwnedFd and safe openat, mkdirat, linkat, renameat, unlinkat, statat, Dir, process_group, and kill_process_group APIs with O_NOFOLLOW and exact resource bounds. Private process groups permit group-wide termination while bounded try_wait observation reaps the owned direct child without an unbounded wait. cargo audit reported no vulnerability for the 47-package lock graph; cargo deny accepted advisories, licenses, sources, and exact rustix 1.1.4 bans; Cargo Vet accepted the exact safe-to-deploy entry.
direct.maintenance: Bytecode Alliance maintains rustix with a published security-reporting process. Exact 1.1.4 is the current reviewed release, declares rust-version 1.63, and documents the required safe fs and process APIs for the registered Apple and Linux targets.
direct.removal: Remove when Rust std provides portable safe descriptor-relative filesystem operations and private-process-group kill support on every registered host.

runner_changes: The active xtask tooling scope participates in risk-gate selection only through its own registered risk_gates set; no application, artifact, or deferred gate is inferred.

One immutable execution context captures bounded adversarial-manifest, quality-registry, integrity-registry, and fixture-harness bytes once; it parses the typed registries once and derives fixture, seed, and schedule identity from those exact bytes. Dependency metadata is streamed into a descriptor-relative create-new no-follow artifact under held root, target, quality, metadata, and attempt directory capabilities; validation reads the same opened inode and rejects any canonical directory or file-name replacement before or after parsing.

EG-CORRECT launches the explicitly registered current-xtask Quality Engineering writer in a private process group with a cleared environment, waits within the registered deadline for an atomically published exact PID and publication-point acknowledgement, sends group-wide termination, reaps the direct child through bounded try_wait observation, launches a distinct recovery process, and accepts only its externally readable predecessor-or-successor state and recovery digest.

EG-FAULT dispatches a closed exhaustive mapping of nine typed adapters for partial-write, process-crash, restart, corruption, bounded-storage, controlled-clock, cancellation, network-publication, and provider-publication schedules. The last five execute a zero-capacity candidate writer that returns typed exhaustion, a two-tick regressed clock consumed by monotonic publication validation, a requested cancellation token consumed by publication, a send through a closed Unix socket, and a send through a closed current-xtask provider-process pipe. Each actual failure persists and synchronizes its bounded error identity separately from the adapter observation. Fresh recovery checks the registered durable-state oracle and candidate shape, reads the operation result, and independently replays the deterministic boundary before accepting it.

EG-INTEGRITY persists identity-bound fixture objects, reopens the golden object, corrupts and deletes attempt-owned copies, requires digest-mismatch and missing-object failures, and proves the untouched prior object remains readable after each adversarial case.

Each gate claims one must-create no-follow fixture root directly beneath the canonical attempt TMPDIR, then performs every fixture create, read, write, copy, link, rename, removal, and recursive cleanup relative to held directory descriptors. Writer and recovery children verify exact device/inode identity tokens before mutation; occupied, symbolic-link, non-directory, escaped, swapped, and identity-changed paths fail closed.

Descriptor-relative open-or-create directory creation falls back to opening an existing entry only when mkdirat returns EEXIST. Parent synchronization, post-create open, durability, permission, resource, and every other error propagate as typed failures and cannot be reclassified by reopening the newly created directory.

An RAII owner reconciles the exact attempt-owned gate tree on success, detector failure, forced writer termination, recovery failure, and timeout; it removes only the identity-owned inode, synchronizes the attempt parent, requires the canonical fixture-root name to be absent, leaves any unowned replacement untouched, and converts replacement or cleanup failure into a failed gate.

All frozen fixture inputs and process records are opened no-follow through their held parent descriptors, checked against their byte ceiling before allocation, read through a maximum-plus-one stream bound into a pre-reserved buffer, and rejected if their opened identity or metadata drifts during the read.
Published fixture process records retain their staged hard link until the attempt-owned RAII cleanup runs, so the acknowledgement does not mutate its own inode metadata after publication.

The internal quality-fixture child interface accepts only its exact registered writer or recovery arity, including parent-claimed directory identities, and rejects any trailing argument before dispatch.

Nextest assigns only copied-workspace tests that source-mutate and rebuild xtask to the source-mutated-fixture-builds resource group with max-threads 2. The rejected 3587d6d PR-profile attempt allowed at least fourteen such builds to overlap: four tests failed after 37-46 seconds and ten reached the unchanged 120-second per-test deadline. Two slots prevented those timeouts while retaining bounded parallelism. Follow-up one-slot and two-slot runs each passed 342 of 343 tests and showed that the remaining bounded-reap assertion was instead counting 20 or more seconds of unrelated pre-seam quality work; that assertion now starts only after an explicit marker from the first injected reap-observer call. Unrelated tests retain normal scheduling and all tests, assertions, retries, status levels, selectors, and deadlines remain unchanged.

EG-TEST retains its exact locked workspace, all-targets, all-features, no-retry CI selection and the existing 131072-byte per-stream ceiling. Its Nextest invocation overrides only live and final status verbosity to failure level, preserves immediate-final failure output from the registered CI profile, requires exactly one terminal canonical summary, rejects missing or ambiguous counts and any skipped test, and retains the completed-test count in the gate detail.

EG-DEPS keeps the 131072-byte controlled stderr ceiling and streams cargo metadata stdout directly into one descriptor-relative create-new attempt-owned artifact capped at 8388608 bytes. The runner reads the same held inode, checks length before allocation, hashes while reading, validates required JSON fields, revalidates every canonical directory and file identity, and records only byte count, digest, device-inode identity, and validation summary in gate capture. Failure cleanup unlinks the artifact only when its canonical name still resolves to that held identity.
unchanged: All 25 gate IDs, stages, coordinators, timeouts, memory declarations, exception classes, targets, thresholds, and application activation ledgers.
The EG-TEST suite selection, failure exit semantics, failure output, retry policy, timeout policy, and controlled stream ceiling.
Developer evidence remains diagnostic and non-merge-eligible.
Release Qualification Cells remain Specified; an engineering runner implementation does not qualify a product artifact.

detection_gained: An active xtask scope can no longer select EG-CORRECT, EG-FAULT, or EG-INTEGRITY and receive an unsupported-runner failure instead of a retained fixture result.

A false predecessor-or-successor oracle, a malformed or oversized fixture registry, and a missing publication-point schedule fail closed through the public quality seam and retain a failed named-gate outcome.
Corrupt fixture bytes are classified as a digest mismatch, deleted fixture objects are classified as missing, and neither adversarial case can mutate or replace its prior persisted object.

The retained report records exact fixture IDs, seeds, fault schedules, writer and recovery process identities, forced termination and bounded reap, externally observed states, recovery digests, typed adapter/injection outcomes, identity-field coverage, and the frozen fixture-registry binding rather than a synthesized cargo self-test verdict.

Mutation after fixture capture cannot alter execution or evidence, dependency metadata directory or file swaps cannot substitute forged bytes, a symlink claim race cannot write outside the attempt root, repeated runs do not accumulate fixture trees, timed-out writer process groups are killed and directly reaped within a fixed bound, and cleanup replacement or failure fails the named gate without deleting an unowned replacement.

Removing the invocation for any one of the nine typed fault adapters fails EG-FAULT through the public quality seam because recovery independently requires that adapter's exact durable observation and candidate-state consequence.

Bypassing any bounded-storage, controlled-clock, cancellation, network-publication, or provider-publication operation while forging its expected observation and error token fails EG-FAULT because the fresh recovery process independently replays the boundary and compares its actual result with the synchronized durable receipt.
A failure synchronizing the parent after descriptor-relative directory creation cannot be reopened and accepted as success; only an exact EEXIST mkdirat result permits the existing-directory path.

The expanded first-class regression inventory cannot exhaust EG-TEST evidence capture through successful per-test status repetition; failures remain visible, successful evidence carries the exact completed-test count with zero skips, and source-mutated copied-workspace builds receive a bounded two-slot resource group without serializing unrelated tests.
The active tooling selection regression test proves EG-CONCURRENCY, EG-CRYPTO, EG-RESOURCE, and EG-SOAK remain explicitly not selected when xtask selects only its registered gates.

Mutable fixture paths are absent from retained reports, and the attempt parent is synchronized after successful removal.
